Friction (0.4 static, 0.3 dynamic) and restitution (0.3) values are set to simulate typical interactions of smooth steel and finished wood with kitchen countertops or pots. For collision detection in Isaac Sim, 'convex_decomposition' is heavily recommended to accurately capture the concavity of the ladle's bowl, which would otherwise be closed off by a standard convex hull. Continuous Collision Detection (CCD) is enabled because the thin-walled geometry can easily tunnel through other objects during fast movements (e.g., stirring or dropping).
